decision_rules.R1_technical_error: A gate/classification whose output contradicts its own documented policy or definition, shown by a unit test, is fixed (smallest change). Fixed: L5 scorecard hard-FAIL on DSR/PSR (duplicate of the L6 gate, called a positive-Sharpe shortfall REJECTED instead of INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE); scorecard NEEDS_MORE_DATA without any FAIL treated as REJECTED.
decision_rules.R2_duplicate: Same statistic and threshold evaluated at two places = one correction counted twice in the list of reasons, no effect on pass/fail: documented, not changed (classification only).
decision_rules.R3_uninformative_gate: Gate G is uninformative if, at the same candidate population, its rejection rate for strong real edges (net Sharpe >= 2, 6y validation) is within 10 percentage points of its rejection rate for null candidates. Such a gate only adds coin-flip noise to the power. Reported; a change needs R4 as well.
decision_rules.R4_double_penalty: Gate G double-penalises the risk that gate H already covers if ALL hold: (a) same risk category in the matrix, (b) P(G rejects | H rejects) >= 0.8 among null/weak candidates, (c) pipeline pass rate of null searches without G does not exceed the Wilson upper bound 2% (no marginal protection: removing G leaves the false-positive rate under 2%) AND the pipeline pass rate without G is not higher than with G by more than the Wilson half-width, (d) removing G raises the power at net Sharpe >= 1.0 by >= 5 pp. Only then G is demoted to 'reported, not deciding'. Otherwise unchanged.
decision_rules.R5_never: No threshold is loosened, no gate is removed because strategies fail it, no strategy passes merely because a gate is absent: a change must keep the pipeline false-positive rate (search level, null cells) <= 2% upper Wilson bound.
